facts.statement: A medium-sized scapulocoracoid found in the Sânpetru Formation likely belonged to an individual with a wingspan of 4.5 to 5 meters.

facts.statement: A single large neck vertebra known as the "RR specimen" or EME 215 was found at the Râpa Roșie locality of the Sebeș Formation.
facts.quote: From the Râpa Roșie locality of the Sebeș Formation, which is contemporary and adjacent to the Densuș-Ciula Formation, a single large neck vertebra, the "RR specimen" or EME 215, was found.

facts.statement: The largest remains indicate a wingspan of 10 to 12 meters, making it one of the biggest pterosaurs.
facts.quote: The largest of these remains indicate it was among the biggest pterosaurs, with an estimated wingspan of 10 to 12 m.

facts.statement: Hatzegopteryx inhabited Hațeg Island, located in the Cretaceous subtropics of the prehistoric Tethys Sea.
facts.quote: Hatzegopteryx inhabited Hațeg Island, an island situated in the Cretaceous subtropics within the prehistoric Tethys Sea.

facts.statement: The wingspan of Quetzalcoatlus northropi was estimated at 11 to 12 meters in 1981.
facts.quote: The wingspan of the latter had been estimated at 11 to 12 m in 1981.

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that a 12-meter wingspan for Hatzegopteryx was conservative, provided its humerus was longer than that of Quetzalcoatlus northropi.
facts.quote: They concluded that an estimate of a 12 m wing span for Hatzegopteryx was conservative, "provided that its humerus was longer than that of Q. northropi".

facts.statement: The wingspan of Hatzegopteryx is generally estimated at 10 to 11 meters.
facts.quote: The latter is generally estimated at 10 to 11 m in length.

facts.statement: The skull was broadened in the rear, measuring 0.5 meters wide across the quadrate bones.
facts.quote: The skull was broadened in the rear, being 0.5 m wide across the quadrate bones.

facts.statement: In 2018, Mátyás Vremir estimated the skull length at 1.6 meters and the wingspan at 8 meters.
facts.quote: In 2018, Mátyás Vremir concluded that Hatzegopteryx likely had a shorter and broader skull, the length of which he estimated at 1.6 m, and he also estimated its wingspan to be smaller than others at 8 m.

facts.statement: The generic name is derived from the Hatzeg basin of Transylvania and the Greek word pteryx meaning "wing".
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Hatzeg (or Hațeg) basin of Transylvania, where the bones were found, and from the Greek word pteryx (πτέρυξ) "wing".

facts.statement: The specific name thambema is derived from the Greek word thambema meaning "terror, monster", referencing its huge size.
facts.quote: The specific name thambema is derived from Greek thambema (θάμβημα) "terror, monster", in reference to its huge size.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the "RR specimen" belongs to Hatzegopteryx thambema due to a lack of overlapping elements, though its bone structure warrants referral to at least H. sp.
facts.quote: Although the lack of overlapping elements prevents this specimen from being definitely referred to Hatzegopteryx thambema, its distinctive internal bone structure, as well as the lack of evidence for a second giant azhdarchid in the area, warrant its referral to at least H. sp.

facts.statement: In 2018, a phylogenetic analysis placed Hatzegopteryx in an advanced position within the family Azhdarchidae.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis conducted by paleontologist Nicholas Longrich and colleagues in 2018 had recovered Hatzegopteryx in a derived (advanced) position within Azhdarchidae.

facts.statement: The genus Hatzegopteryx was named by Buffetaut, Grigorescu, and Csiki in 2002.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Buffetaut, Grigorescu & Csiki, 2002

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Hatzegopteryx thambema, also described in 2002.
facts.quote: subdivision: Hatzegopteryx thambema Buffetaut, Grigorescu & Csiki, 2002 (tipo)

facts.statement: Despite its unusually large and robust skull, Hatzegopteryx was not flightless, as its wing bones resemble those of other flying pterosaurs.
facts.quote: The skull of Hatzegopteryx was unusually large and robust, its wing bones are comparable to those of other flying pterosaurs, indicating that it was not flightless at all.

facts.statement: To support flight, the skull bones of Hatzegopteryx contained internal hollows up to 10 mm long separated by thin bony struts.
facts.quote: The necessary weight reduction may have been accomplished by the internal structure of the skull bones, which were full of small pits and hollows (alveoli) up to 10 mm long, separated by a matrix of thin bony struts (trabeculae).

facts.statement: The internal bone structure of Hatzegopteryx resembles expanded polystyrene, making the skull sturdy yet lightweight.
facts.quote: This unusual construction differs from that of other pterosaurs, and more closely resembles the structure of expanded polystyrene (which is used to manufacture Styrofoam).

facts.statement: The posterior neck vertebrae of Hatzegopteryx could withstand between five and ten times its body weight.
facts.quote: the posterior neck vertebrae of Hatzegopteryx can withstand anywhere between five and ten body weights, depending on the loading of the bone.

facts.statement: Hatzegopteryx was likely a terrestrial generalist predator, similar to other azhdarchid pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Paleoecology Like all azhdarchid pterosaurs, Hatzegopteryx was probably a terrestrially foraging generalist predator.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Hatzegopteryx acted as an apex predator in the Hațeg Island ecosystem due to its large size.
facts.quote: it has been suggested that Hatzegopteryx played the role of an apex predator in the Hațeg Island ecosystem.

facts.statement: Its robust anatomy suggests Hatzegopteryx could prey on animals too large to swallow whole, unlike other giant azhdarchids.
facts.quote: The robust anatomy of Hatzegopteryx suggests that it may have tackled larger prey than other azhdarchids, including animals too large to swallow whole.

facts.statement: Hatzegopteryx lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Hatzegopteryx lived on the Tisia–Dacia Block, an island landmass that included the Hațeg Basin.
facts.quote: The members of the Hațeg Island ecosystem lived on a landmass known as the Tisia–Dacia Block, of which the Hațeg Basin was a small part.

facts.statement: The island habitat of Hatzegopteryx had a subtropical climate with an average temperature of about 25°C.
facts.quote: Being located at 27°N, the island was located farther south than the present-day latitude of 45°N. As such, the climate was likely subtropical, with distinct dry and wet seasons, and had an average temperature of about 25 C.

facts.statement: It is debated whether similarities between Hatzegopteryx and Quetzalcoatlus northropi indicate synonymy, as the humerus is considered non-diagnostic for giant azhdarchids.
facts.quote: However, this is likely due to the relatively non-diagnostic nature of the humerus in giant azhdarchid taxonomy and the lack of a detailed description for the elements of Q. northropi at the time of the assignment.

facts.statement: Hatzegopteryx is an extinct genus of azhdarchid pterosaur known from incomplete remains found in Transylvania, Romania.
facts.quote: Hatzegopteryx (cuyo nombre significa "ala de la cuenca Hațeg") es un género extinto de pterosaurio azdárquido, conocido de restos incompletos hallados en Transilvania, en Rumania.

facts.statement: Hatzegopteryx was among the largest pterosaurs, with a wingspan estimated at 10 to 12 meters.
facts.quote: Los fragmentos del cráneo, el húmero izquierdos, y otros restos fosilizados indican que estuvo entre los mayores pterosaurios, con una envergadura de 10-12 metros

facts.statement: Hatzegopteryx had a shorter, more robust, and muscular neck compared to other azhdarchids.
facts.quote: pero con un cuello más corto, robusto y más musculado en comparación con otros azdárquidos

facts.statement: The only known species of Hatzegopteryx is the type species Hatzegopteryx thambema.
facts.quote: La especie tipo y única conocida es Hatzegopteryx thambema.

facts.statement: In the absence of large theropods, Hatzegopteryx was likely the apex predator of the Hațeg Island ecosystem during the Late Cretaceous, hunting prey proportionally larger than other azhdarchids.
facts.quote: En ausencia de terópodos grandes, Hatzegopteryx fue probablemente el superdepredador del ecosistema insular de la isla de Hațeg durante el Cretácico Superior, atacando a presas proporcionalmente mayores que las de otros azdárquidos.

facts.statement: The first remains of Hatzegopteryx were found in the upper part of the Densuș Ciula Formation in Vălioara, Romania, dated to the Late Maastrichtian about 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Hatzegopteryx fueron encontrados en la zona superior de la Formación Densuș Ciula en Vălioara, al noroeste de la Cuenca de Hațeg, en Transilvania, al oeste de Rumania, la cual ha sido data de finales de la época del Maastrichtiense del período Cretácico, hace unos 66 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen FGGUB R 1083A consists of two fragments of the back of the skull and the damaged proximal part of a left humerus.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Hatzegopteryx, FGGUB R 1083A, consiste de dos fragmentos de la parte posterior del cráneo y la parte proximal dañada de un húmero izquierdo.

facts.statement: A 38.5 cm long femur fragment found nearby, FGGUB R1625, may have belonged to Hatzegopteryx.
facts.quote: Una sección media de 38,5 centímetros de largo de un fémur hallado cerca, FGGUB R1625, puede haber pertenecido a Hatzegopteryx.

facts.statement: If FGGUB R1625 belonged to Hatzegopteryx, it likely represented a smaller individual with a wingspan of 5 to 6 meters.
facts.quote: FGGUB R1625 pudo haber pertenecido a un individuo más pequeño de Hatzegopteryx (asumiendo que pertenezca a este género), con una envergadura de 5 - 6 metros.

facts.statement: A medium-sized scapulocoracoid found at the Vadu locality likely belonged to an individual with a wingspan of 4.5 to 5 meters.
facts.quote: De la localidad de Vadu, se halló un escapulocoracoides mediano, el cual probablemente pertenecía a un individuo con una envergadura de 4,5 - 5 metros.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2002 by French paleontologist Eric Buffetaut and Romanian paleontologists Dan Grigorescu and Zoltan Csiki.
facts.quote: El género fue nombrado en 2002 por el paleontólogo francés Eric Buffetaut, y los paleontólogos rumanos Dan Grigorescu y Zoltan Csiki.

facts.statement: The generic name derives from the Hațeg Basin in Transylvania, where the bones were found, and the Greek word for 'wing'.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva de la cuenca Hatzeg (o Hațeg) de Transilvania, la así llamada isla de Hațeg, donde sus huesos fueron hallados, y del término griego pteryx (ἡ πτέρυξ, -υγος (también ἡ πτερύξ, -ῦγος), es decir "ala".

facts.statement: The species name thambema comes from the Greek word for 'monster' or 'terror', referring to its enormous size.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie thambema se deriva de la palabra griega para "monstruo" o "terror" (τό θάμβημα, -ήματος), en referencia a su enorme tamaño.

facts.statement: Hatzegopteryx apparently had a robust skull expanded at the back and an enormous jaw.
facts.quote: Hatzegopteryx aparentemente tenía un robusto cráneo ampliado en la parte posterior, y una enorme mandíbula.

facts.statement: Buffetaut and colleagues estimated the skull of Hatzegopteryx was nearly three meters long, making it larger than the largest Quetzalcoatlus species and one of the largest skulls of any non-marine animal.
facts.quote: Buffetaut y colegas en su descripción inicial de los especímenes estimaron que el cráneo de Hatzegopteryx era probablemente de casi tres metros de largo, lo que lo haría mayor que el de la mayor especie de Quetzalcoatlus y entre los mayores cráneos de cualquier animal no marino.

facts.statement: The skull bones of Hatzegopteryx were solid and robust, featuring large areas scored for muscle insertion.
facts.quote: En Hatzegopteryx, los huesos del cráneo son sólidos y robustos, con grandes áreas surcadas de inserción muscular.

facts.statement: Researchers theorized that necessary weight reduction was achieved through an internal bone structure filled with small pits over 10 mm long, separated by an incredibly thin matrix of bone struts, a feature also found in some wing bones.
facts.quote: Los autores teorizaron que la reducción de peso necesaria fue lograda por la estructura interna de los huesos craneales, la cual estaba llena de pequeños fosos y huecos (alvéolos) de más de 10 milímetros de largo, separados por una matriz de puntales de hueso increíblemente delgados (trabéculos), una característica también hallada en algunas partes de los huesos alares de Hatzegopteryx.

facts.statement: Researchers noted this unusual structure could have allowed a strong, tension-resistant constitution that remained lightweight, enabling this large-headed animal to fly.
facts.quote: Ellos notaron que esto pudo haber permitido una fuerte constitución resistente a las tensiones sin dejar de ser liviana, lo que a su vez le habría permitido a este animal de gran cabeza volar.

facts.statement: A large cervical vertebra attributed to Hatzegopteryx is short and unusually robust, with the preserved section measuring 240 mm and the whole vertebra estimated at 300 mm.
facts.quote: Una gran vértebra cervical atribuida a Hatzegopteryx es corta e inusualmente robusta. La sección preservada mide 240 milímetros de largo, estimándose que la vértebra entera mediría probablemente 300 milímetros de longitud.

facts.statement: While similar vertebrae in Arambourgiania would measure 2,652 mm, indicating that Hatzegopteryx's neck was only 50-60% the length expected for an azhdarchid of its size.
facts.quote: Entretanto, esas mismas vértebras en Arambourgiania, un pterosaurio de tamaño similar, medirían 2,652 metros; esto indica que el cuello de Hatzegopteryx tiene un 50-60% de la longitud que sería esperable para un azdárquido de su talla.

facts.statement: The lower surface of the cervical vertebra is unusually thick, measuring between 4 and 6 mm.
facts.quote: La superficie inferior de la vértebra cervical es además inusualmente gruesa, midiendo entre 4 a 6 milímetros.

facts.statement: In their 2002 description, Buffetaut and colleagues suggested the skull weight must have been reduced in an unconventional way to allow flight, though they admitted it could have been a non-flying animal, finding this unlikely due to similarities in wing bones with flying pterosaurs.
facts.quote: En su descripción de 2002, Buffetaut y colegas sugirieron que para poder volar, el peso del cráneo debía de haber estar reducido en alguna forma no convencional (aunque ellos admitían que pudo haber sido un animal no volador, lo encontraron poco probable debido a las similitudes de sus huesos alares con los de otros pterosaurios voladores).

facts.statement: Although initially identified as a third cervical vertebra, a set of traits supports its identification as a vertebra from the posterior neck, specifically the seventh vertebra.
